t: Looking up, you see Newton, a large bronze sculpture on a high plinth in the piazza outside the British Library. It dates from 1995 and is the work of Eduardo Paolozzi, a Scottish artist widely regarded as a pioneer of pop art. It is sometimes known as Newton after Blake. The figure depicts Isaac Newton, the mathematician and physicist whose Principia, published in 1687, established classical mechanics. Newton also made major contributions to optics and shares credit for developing calculus. It's a fitting figure to greet people arriving at a great library.
